newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called lower after July expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called lower after July expiry.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open lower Thursday after July expiry that showed some weakness on generation unit returns and bearish weather in the Pacific Northwest,
"You have units coming back, mild weather and natural gas coming off, power is following," a West Coast broker said.

August Palo Verde (PV) futures, in over-the-counter (OTC) business, were quoted at $33.60-34.15 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Wednesday's settlement at $34.33 and August California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were talked $22.20-22.70 against yesterday's close of $23.10.
In other OTC activity, July PV power was discussed at $31.75-32.25 and August COB $19.50-20.00.
Forecasters called for cooler-than-normal weather across the Pacific Northwest but normal to hotter-than-normal conditions in the Southwest in the next six to ten days
The 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 2 nuclear power unit reached 98 percent power early Thursday after dropping to 60 percent due to a low pressure feedwater heater outage.
Traders said the market would be watchful of next week's scheduled return of the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state and 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear unit in southern California.

Several Western coal-fired power units are expected to be put back to the grid beginning today, including a 300 MW Reid Gardner unit in Las Vegas, Nevada, a 670 MW unit at Centralia, Wash., 330 MW Colstrip unit in Montana and 260 MW Hayden unit Colorado.
On the downside, analysts assessed technical support for August PV at $32.00 and August COB $22.00-22.45.
